Command file structure convention (formerly US-063) is documented in docs/command-structure.md: every src/RoslynTools.Cli/Commands/*Command.cs file follows the order — using directives, namespace, class declaration with IRtCommand, public static readonly Info field, public static Command Build() method, private static handler method(s), no other top-level declarations.
Convention: handler methods live inside the Command class as private static methods; no separate service classes; service logic stays in src/RoslynTools/Services/ and src/RoslynTools/Core/.
Convention: Build() is at most 60 lines; if a Build() exceeds that, split option construction into private static methods.

Architecture ratchet (formerly US-064) in tests/RoslynTools.Tests/Architecture/CommandFileStructureTests.cs: a marker file docs/structure-migrated-commands.txt lists commands that have been migrated to the canonical structure; the test asserts every listed command passes the structure invariants (Info first, Build second, no other public members, no top-level statements).
Architecture ratchet: a separate test enforces the marker file only grows — never shrinks. Removing a command from the marker file requires deleting the corresponding Command class.

Architecture ratchet: when all commands in src/RoslynTools.Cli/Commands/ are in the marker file, the test transitions from ratchet mode to enforcement mode (asserts ALL commands pass without consulting the marker).

Migration playbook (formerly US-066) in docs/command-migration-playbook.md: a concise (under 200 lines) document with sections: (1) when to use the playbook, (2) the 8-step migration sequence — read existing command, identify hand-rolled options to replace, migrate to CommandOptionFactory, restructure Build() to canonical order, add Info metadata fields (Aliases/SeeAlso/SupportedFormats), add structure-migrated-commands.txt entry, run rt dump-help to verify, ship; (3) what NOT to do during migration (no behaviour changes, no AC changes, no test refactoring beyond what the structure ratchet requires); (4) how to back out if a migration breaks.
Playbook references the option factory contract from US-084 (formerly US-058+US-062) and the metadata contract from US-083 (formerly US-059+RT-001+US-065).

First command migration demonstrates the playbook end-to-end: pick one simple read-only command (e.g. OutlineCommand or DescribeCommand), apply all 8 steps, land as a separate commit that the playbook references as the canonical example.
dotnet build clean; dotnet format --verify-no-changes clean; existing tests pass; new architecture tests green.
Architecture test exposes a `ListUnmigratedCommands` helper that prints the remaining commands when run — useful for future migration sweeps.
